hooks.A: What if the Moon disappeared tonight? The scariest change wouldn't be the dark sky.
hooks.C: What if the Moon just vanished? Earth's oceans, animals, and even seasons would change.

lines.text: First, the night would get a lot darker. The Moon is the brightest thing in our night sky.
Next, the oceans. The Moon's gravity causes most of Earth's tides.
Without it, only the Sun would pull on the seas, and tides would get much weaker.
Tide pools, coastlines, and the animals living there would be thrown off.
Some corals even use moonlight as a signal to spawn, all on the same night.
But the scariest change is slow. The Moon keeps Earth's tilt steady.
Today it only wobbles between about twenty two and twenty four and a half degrees.
Without the Moon, scientists estimate the tilt could swing anywhere from zero to forty five degrees.
That could mean wild seasons: freezing in some places, scorching in others.
And our days? The Moon has been slowly making them longer, by about two milliseconds every century.
Without it, that slowdown would mostly stop.
So the Moon isn't just pretty. It helps keep Earth a stable place to live.
Now look up tonight, and imagine the sky without it.
